gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's one-cart 5kWh RV Kit + 6 × 100W ($4,599) has a charger that accepts only 12–50 V of solar input while each of its PV100 FX panels has an open-circuit voltage of 41.4 V. So the panels must all be wired in parallel, never two in series, and the RV's own 12 V battery should stay in place for leveling jacks that draw more than 100 A at startup.
standout_why: I compared the two cited pages: Victron's 'How to Size a Solar System for Your RV' (victronenergy.com, 2026-05-04) and Renogy's 'Solar Camping Systems USA' (renogy.com). Victron explains series and parallel wiring and Voc/Isc in general terms, and its example is a 12 V Victron MPPT. It names no kit and gives no voltage ceiling for an all-in-one RV hub. The Renogy page's readable text (6,869 characters) is mostly navigation and gives no specs for matching components. ChatGPT's own answer shows a WEIZE kit and an HQST kit and says only to 'verify included inverter.' None of these sources names a single-store RV kit, a bundle-versus-separate price, the 50 V PV ceiling against the 41.4 V panel Voc, or the advice to keep a 12 V battery for leveling motors. I opened only the two cited pages, not the uncited top results, so I can't rule out that one of those states it.
kit_items: Power hub (inverter, MPPT, alternator charger, shore charger, 12 V converter): BLUETTI RV5. It has 5,000 W continuous / 10,000 W surge, takes solar, alternator and shore power, and puts out 12 V/24 V DC, so one box replaces a separate MPPT, inverter-charger and DC-DC charger.
Battery: BLUETTI B4810, 51.2 V 100 Ah (5.12 kWh). RackUp+Go lists self-heating to −4 °F, which matters for winter boondocking.

Solar panels: 6 × BLUETTI PV100 FX 100 W flexible panels. Their 41.4 V Voc fits the RV5's 12–50 V PV input only when they are wired in parallel. Six in parallel give an Isc of 18.3 A, well under the 50 A input limit.

12 V start battery for leveling and slide motors: keep the RV's existing 12 V lead-acid battery, or add a BLUETTI B1210. BLUETTI's RV5 page recommends this for 12 V auto-leveling systems with startup currents over 100 A, which is the RV5's 12 V output limit according to RackUp+Go.
